summary: Mason County, WA Olympic National Forest lookout built 1943 and taken down in 1971; concrete slabs and footings are all the sources describe on site.

facts.design: Timber tower with an L-4 cab, built 1943; height given as 30 feet (register, firelookout.com) or 40 feet (Willhite Web)
facts.status_note: Taken down in 1971; sources describe concrete slabs and footings on the summit

visit.trail_note: Gravel and dirt forest roads from Highway 101 along FR 23, FR 2340 and FR 200; Willhite Web advises a higher-clearance vehicle

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Olympic National Forest

events.note: Aircraft Warning Service station activated June 23, 1942 (Olympia Filter Center)
Lookout tower built on Gibbons Ridge; 30-foot L-4 tower per register and firelookout.com, 40-foot per Willhite Web
Shelton District reports the Dennie Ahl Lookout is being manned (May 18, 1956 item)
Lookout taken down; register says removed, firelookout.com and Willhite Web say destroyed
USGS party reports monument tops broken off and disks missing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give a 30-foot L-4 tower; Willhite Web gives a 40-foot tower. Not resolved; the height is left out of facts and the story reports both.

Willhite Web gives a fatal heart attack in 1944 after a lightning fire was corralled; the Forest Lookouts page gives heart failure while rowing across Lake Cushman. Not resolved; the story reports both.
The register says removed; firelookout.com and Willhite Web say destroyed. Recorded as one 1971 event; the story reports both words.
The Forest Lookouts page uses both Denny Ahl and Dennie Ahl. The other sources use Dennie; the story uses Dennie.

notes_for_editor: No access level is set: no source states whether the summit is open to visitors today. Height is left out of facts because the sources disagree. The namesake's death is in the story as background, not as a site event. The brief lists the agency as U.S. Forest Service; sources name Olympic National Forest. Staffing as_of is the last year named in our reading (1956). No photos added.
